title: Invert Binary Tree
description: Swap each node’s left and right children, then recursively invert both subtrees. Return the original root.
note: TreeNode? permits a node or none. The explicit absence check makes field access safe; swap! exchanges the child references.
notes: LeetCode supplies TreeNode. The record declaration shows how the same type would be defined in a standalone Birdie program.
Returning early after root == none narrows root to TreeNode in the remaining body. Its children remain optional, so recursive calls accept TreeNode?.

Records are shared references. swap!(root.left, root.right) exchanges the writable child fields, mutates the original tree, and allocates no replacement nodes. Tuple assignment can also express the exchange: (root.left, root.right) = (root.right, root.left).
An empty tree returns none. A leaf is unchanged. The traversal takes O(n) time and O(h) recursion space, where h is the tree height.
